name: Reed Hastings
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2015-2025); Hurun Global (2017-2026); Wikidata (2025); SEC insider holdings (2026)
forbes_bio: Reed Hastings, cofounder and chairman of Netflix, revolutionized how the world is entertained.
Hastings cofounded Netflix in 1997, the same year he sold his first company, Pure Software. He took Netflix public in 2002.
Netflix originally operated as a DVD-by-mail subscription service, but began streaming content in 2007.
Hastings stepped down as co-CEO in 2023 and has been reducing his shareholding; he now owns less than 1% of Netflix shares.
In 2020, he and his wife Patty donated $120 million to two historically Black colleges and the United Negro College Fund. Their lifetime giving surpasses $2 billion.
forbes_facts: The son of a Nixon administration lawyer, Hastings studied math at Bowdoin College and served in the Peace Corps in Swaziland.
Hastings holds a graduate degree in artificial intelligence from Stanford.

name: Lawrence Stroll
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2012-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); Wikidata (2021)
forbes_bio: Lawrence Stroll masterminded Michael Kors' hugely successful IPO in 2011 with business partner Silas Chou, a Hong Kong fashion tycoon.
The bulk of Stroll's fortune comes from selling his shares in the American fashion brand; he sold the last of his stake in 2014.
In Aug. 2018, Stroll led a group of investors to buy Formula One racing team Force India for £90 million plus assumption of £15 million in debt.
After leading a $235.6 million (£182 million) investment in Aston Martin in early 2020, Stroll became executive chairman of the car company.
As part of the deal, Stroll's Formula One team, Racing Point, was rebranded as the Aston Martin Team, marking the brand's return to Formula One after 60 years.
His 23-year-old son, Lance Stroll--one of the youngest members to compete in Formula One--drives for Aston Martin.
forbes_facts: Stroll collects vintage Ferraris, one of which he purchased for a record-breaking $27.5 million in 2013.
Stroll's real last name, which appeared on documents to buy Force India, is Strulovitch.

name: Anthony Wood
sec_insider_companies: ROKU, INC (ROKU) - CEO and Chairman BOD
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2019-2025); Hurun Global (2020-2026); Wikidata (2021); SEC insider holdings (2026)
forbes_bio: Anthony Wood is the founder and CEO of Roku, a tech company that lets users stream content on their TVs.
He launched Roku in 2002 after selling his previous business, ReplayTV, to SONICblue.
Roku went public on the Nasdaq in 2017.
Wood received his bachelor's in electrical engineering from Texas A&M after moving to the U.S. from Manchester, England as a child.
Throughout his early life, Wood was always making things: building tree houses in elementary school and writing software in high school.
forbes_facts: Wood was an early innovator of DVR.

name: Ursula Hutter-Schleicher
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2025); Hurun Global (2026)
forbes_bio: Ursula Hutter-Schleicher derives her fortune from Schwenk cement, one of Germany's oldest family-owned businesses founded in 1847.
Today the company, which employs 4,500 people, supplies the construction industry with cement, concrete, sand and gravel.
Her brother Eduard Schleicher manages the company and is also a billionaire.

name: D. Leopoldo Del Pino
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes real-time (former) (2021); Forbes annual (2013-2025)
forbes_bio: Leopoldo del Pino y Calvo Sotelo inherited a stake in Ferrovial S.A., Spain's largest infrastructure construction and management company.
His father, who founded the company in 1952, died in 2008. Leopoldo's two siblings also inherited stakes in Ferrovial.
Leopoldo's brother Rafael del Pino is the chairman and co-CEO of Ferrovial.
Leopoldo, who owns about 4% of Ferrovial, served as a board member of the company until early 2016.

name: Bom Kim
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2020-2025); Hurun Global (2022-2026); Wikidata (2025); Hurun Unicorn founders (2019-2020)
forbes_bio: Bom Kim is the founder of South Korean internet giant Coupang, which went public on the New York Stock Exchange in 2021 and is now headquartered in Seattle.
Mimicking U.S.-based Amazon, Coupang is disrupting South Korea's online retail space by slashing prices and investing heavily in swift deliveries.
In 2018, it raised $2 billion from SoftBank's Vision Fund at a $9 billion valuation, making it Korea's most valuable privately-held startup.
The 2021 IPO of Coupang was the biggest U.S. listing of an Asian company since Alibaba in 2014.
forbes_facts: Kim worked at Boston Consulting Group before founding Vintage Media Company, which he sold in 2009. He started Coupang the next year.
Kim is a graduate of Harvard University; He later attended Harvard Business School but dropped out after only six months.

name: John Phillips
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2021-2025); Hurun Global (2024-2026)
forbes_bio: John Phillips is an angel investor who made an early bet on Shopify, a Canadian e-commerce software company.
He and his wife Catherine Phillips together own an estimated 2% of Shopify.
John served on Shopify's board of directors from 2010 to 2023.
The couple has invested in a slew of other early-stage companies that are lesser known, like Virtual Marine Technology and Sequence Bio.
John previously spent 25 years as a corporate lawyer, including as general counsel at telecom firm Clearnet Communications.
The Phillips' Northpine Foundation has donated hundreds of millions to organizations focused on climate, refugees and formerly incarcerated individuals.

name: Athanasios Martinos
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2024-2025); Hurun Global (2025-2026)
forbes_bio: Athanasios Martinos is the owner of Greek shipping firm Eastern Mediterranean Maritime, which has a fleet of 75 tankers, bulk carriers and container vessels.
He founded the company in 1990, after splitting from the family shipping company Thenamaris, which he had cofounded with his mother and two brothers in 1972.
Collectively, Athanasios and his brothers Andreas and Constantinos own the largest shipping fleet in Greece, the largest shipowning nation in the world.
He also owns a Cyprus-based real estate investment firm which holds office and retail properties in London and Geneva.
He served as the civil administrator of the monastic community of Mount Athos, an autonomous region run by Orthodox monks in Greece, from 2019 to 2023.

name: David Kabiller
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2017-2020); Hurun Global (2018-2021)
forbes_bio: David Kabiller is a cofounder and head of business development at AQR, a quantitative investment firm with $187 billion in assets under management.
AQR stands for Applied Quantitative Research. It invests based on quantitative and proprietary signals, offering products including hedge funds, mutual funds and separately managed accounts.
The firm is headquartered in Greenwich, Connecticut, with other locations in Bangaluru, Dubai, Hong Kong, London, Munich and Sydney.
Before AQR, he was a vice president at Goldman Sachs, working with chief investment officers of large pension and endowment funds in North America.
forbes_facts: Kabiller founded the Kabiller Prize and the Kabiller Young Investigator Award for researchers in nanoscience and nanomedicine at Northwestern University.
At Northwestern, his alma mater, Kabiller has founded a series of prizes and awards in the field of nanoscience and nanomedicine.
